QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r7.claim: “Best” can mean simply good, or the superlative: good is what knowledge permits and the best is more fitting and correct.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r7.anchor: وفيه قولان ؛ أحدهما أن يكون بمعنى الحسن

QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r8.claim: The best speech is what is done for God alone or pure remembrance of Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r8.anchor: ويقال الأحسن ما كان لله دون غيره

QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r9.claim: Inner promptings come from the self, Satan, an angel, or the Real, and each source calls toward a different response.
QUSHAYRI:v3p115/r9.anchor: هواجس النفس ووساوس الشيطان وخواطر الملك وخطاب الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r11.claim: The explicit noun “servants” replaces a pronoun to identify the promised group and introduce their quality of listening carefully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r11.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر ليدل على أنهم هم، وليترتب على الظاهر الوصف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r12.claim: The “saying” is general and they follow its best; another view takes it as the Qur'an, especially its teachings of pardon and forbearance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p191#2/r12.anchor: وهو عام في جميع الأقوال، فيتبعون أحسنه: ثناء عليهم بنفوذ بصائرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r1.claim: Qatada says the best saying is obedience to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r1.anchor: وقال قتادة: أحسن القول طاعة الله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas describes someone who hears good and bad reports in a gathering, passes on the best, and leaves the rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: هو الرجل يجلس مع القوم، فيسمع الحديث فيه محاسن ومساو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r3.claim: The phrase “who listen to speech” may be an adjective of “servants”; alternatively, one may pause after “servants” and make “those who” a new subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p192/r3.anchor: والذين: وصف لعباد. وقيل: الوقف على عباد، والذين مبتدأ خبره أولئك

THALABI:v8p226/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p226/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p226/r8.claim: The best saying is the one that most rightly guides its hearer to truth.
THALABI:v8p226/r8.anchor: فبشر عباد الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أرشده وأهداه إلى الحق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r4.claim: Those who listen to speech and follow its best part follow the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:15-20/r4.anchor: { الذين يستمعون القول } القرآن وغيره { فيتبعون أحسنه } وهو القرآن

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.claim: Believers receive glad tidings; the Prophet's call appeals to people of understanding, and he is not responsible for those whose deeds make them fuel for Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p531/r6.anchor: his call will only appeal to men of understanding; it is not his responsibility to guide those who have become the fuel of Hell

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r3.claim: The upright listen carefully instead of responding aggressively, then follow every sound thing said to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r3.anchor: instead of fighting and showing aggression to the person who presents them his views, listen carefully to him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r4.claim: Their upright, truth-loving attitude makes them value the Qur’an as guidance, and God grants them that guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r4.anchor: they valued the Qur’ān revealed by the Almighty as guidance to mankind and God blessed them with this guidance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r5.claim: Only people of understanding benefit from God’s reminder; this restates 39:9 and parallels the reminder for people of understanding in Sūrah Ṣād.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p539/r5.anchor: it is these people who are men of understanding and only such people can benefit from God’s reminder

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.claim: For colors and bodily defects, Arabic does not form ما أفعله exclamatives; it uses ما أشد plus the noun, as in ما أشد حمرته.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.anchor: ولا تقول في الأعرج ما أعرجه ولا في الأعشى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.claim: If ما أفعله is unavailable for a quality, the corresponding أفعل به and أفعل منه constructions are unavailable too, since these forms share the same scalar sense.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.anchor: وما لم يكن فيه ما أفعله لم يكن فيه أفعل به رجلا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.claim: Al-Khalil explains the restriction by saying colors and bodily defects are treated like body parts, so speakers say ما أشد يده rather than ما أيده.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.anchor: الخليل أنهم إنما منعهم من أن يقولوا في هذه ما أفعله

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.claim: These bodily qualities do not take مفعال or فعول forms; such forms instead intensify an action or quality, like ضروب and محسان.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.anchor: كما تقول رجل ضروب ورجل محسان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.claim: ما أحمقه, ما أرعنه, ما أنوكه, and ما ألده are allowed because these qualities concern reason and discernment rather than bodily form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.anchor: ما أنوكه وفي الألد ما ألده فإنما هذا عندهم من العلم ونقصان العقل والفطنة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.claim: These mental traits are treated like other character judgments, such as foolishness and courage, rather than physical defects.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.anchor: فصارت ما ألده بمنزلة ما أمرسه وما أعلمه وصارت ما أحمقه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.claim: The same permission applies to أهوج, as in ما أهوجه, because it is a mental disposition rather than bodily shape.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالايجوزفيهماأفعله)#704/.anchor: وكذلك الأهوج تقول ما أهوجه كقولك ما أجنه

SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r1.claim: The apparent parsing makes الذين يستمعون an adjective of عبادي; it may instead be بدل or explanatory apposition.
SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه نعت لعبادي، أو بدل منه، أو بيان له.

SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r2.claim: Alternatively, الذين يستمعون is a new subject with أولئك الذين as predicate; stop at عبادي and resume after it.
SAMIN-DURR:39:18/r2.anchor: وقيل: يجوز أن يكون مبتدأ. وقوله: { أولئك الذين } إلخ خبره. وعلى هذا فالوقف على قوله: " عبادي " والابتداء بما بعده.

ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r2.claim: One reading of the phrase is that they listen to the Qur’an and other speech, then follow the Qur’an as the best of it.
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r2.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون يستمعون القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن

ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r3.claim: Alternatively, they hear all God’s commands and follow the best course, such as choosing pardon over retaliation; forgiving a claim one could pursue earns greater reward.
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r3.anchor: وجائز أن يكونوا يستمعون جميع ما أمر الله به فيتبعون أحسن ذلك نحو القصاص والعفو

ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r1.claim: Razi reads the verse as praising reasoned scrutiny of religious propositions, acceptance of what reason validates, and rejection of what fails its test.
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r1.anchor: According to Razi, this describes people who examine every religious proposition (in the widest sense of this term) in the light of their own reason

ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r2.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r2.claim: Tabari advances a similar reading of reasoned examination, though in simpler terms.
ASAD-NOTES:39:14#n22/r2.anchor: A somewhat similar view is advanced, albeit in simpler terms, by Tabari.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported with عبادي and a fatḥa on its yāʾ; ʿUbayd says he pauses at an āya ending and otherwise connects عبادي الذين, calling this the separated reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ أبو عمرو وحده: فبشر عبادي. الذين [الزمر/ 17، 18] بنصب الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأهل مكة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.claim: The al-Qaṭʿī transmission from ʿUbayd and Shibl reports Ibn Kathīr and the people of Mecca with عبادي and fatḥa on the yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r2.anchor: القطعي عن عبيد عن شبل عن ابن كثير وأهل مكة: فبشر عبادي. الذين بنصب الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.speaker: قنبل
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.claim: Qunbul, from al-Nabbāl and Ibn Kathīr’s associates, reads عباد الذين without yāʾ, with kasra on the dāl.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r3.anchor: وقرأت على قنبل عن النبال عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير: عباد. الذين بكسر الدال من غير ياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.claim: The remaining readers read عباد الذين without a yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: عباد. الذين بغير ياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.claim: Al-Fārisī considers both leaving the yāʾ quiescent and vocalizing it acceptable.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p93#2/r5.anchor: التسكين في الياء حسن، والتحريك فيها أيضا حسن

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jinnī marks where a report from Abu ʿAlī ends and his own analysis begins, using formulas that introduce his independent view.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r1.anchor: ثم يقول: هذا آخر الحكاية عن أبي علي، وينتقل إلى إضافة ما يريد أن يضيف، مما يستقل به من رأي

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jinnī trusts Ibn Mujāhid as a transmitter of reports and readings, while freely opposing his linguistic judgments.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p16#2/r7.anchor: ونقل عن ابن مجاهد فوثق به في النقل والرواية، وتعقبه في اللغة بالإنكار والمخالفة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r1.claim: The verse praises people who critically distinguish good from better in religion, choosing obligation over recommendation and recommendation over what is merely permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r1.anchor: مدح لهم بأنهم نقاد في الدين يميزون بين الحسن والأحسن والفاضل والأفضل

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r2.claim: One interpretation is that they follow the better of God's two available commands, such as retaliation or pardon, taking revenge or forbearance, and disclosure or concealment.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r2.anchor: وقيل يستععون القول أو أمر الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r3.claim: This choice-based reading is narrower: it concerns commands with a choice between options; the first reading more broadly selects the better of any two statements, such as obligation over recommendation.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r3.anchor: والفرق بين الوجهين أن هذا أخص لأنه مخصوص بأوامر فيها تخيير بين راجح كالعفو والقصاص مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says they hear the Quran and other speech, then follow the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r4.anchor: وعن الزجاج يستمعون القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r5.claim: Another view says they listen to whoever speaks and follow what is most worthy of acceptance and best guides to truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r5.anchor: وقيل يستمعون القول ممن كان فيتبعون أولاه بالقبول وأرشده إلى الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r6.claim: These worshippers are the people who shunned ṭāghūt and turned to God, preserving the passage's continuity between the glad tidings and the command to convey them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r6.anchor: وأريد بهؤلاء العباد الذين اجتنبوا وأنابوا لا غيرهم لئلا ينفك النظم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r8.claim: A proposed pause after ʿibādī makes the relative clause a new subject, with “those are the ones God guided” as its predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r8.anchor: وقيل الوقف ( عبادي ) فيكون الذين مبتدأ خبره جملة قوله تعالى ( أولئك الذين هداهم الله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers attaching the relative clause to the previous description: replacing the pronoun and completing the thought support it, and it better answers the question prompted by following the best speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r9.anchor: وما تقدم أرجح لما سلف من الفوائد من إقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر والتتميم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r10.claim: People of sound intellect are free from the opposition of delusion and the struggle of caprice, and they alone deserve guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r10.anchor: أي هم أصحاب العقول السليمة عن معارضة الوهم ومنازعة الهوى المستحقون للهداية لا غيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r11.claim: The verse indicates the low standing of blind imitation; a cited poem urges striving as a religious reasoner rather than following passively like a tethered camel.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r11.anchor: ولذا قيل : شمر وكن في أمور الدين مجتهدا ولا تكن مثل عير قيد فانقادا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r12.claim: The verse is used to support the Ashʿarī position that guidance results from God's act together with the soul's acceptance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p252#3/r12.anchor: واستدل بها على أن الهداية تحصل بفعل الله تعالى وقبول النفس لها كما ذهب إليه الأشاعرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r1.claim: Al-qawl, the speech they hear, is the Qur'an.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r1.anchor: {الذين يستمعون القول} القرآن، {فيتبعون أحسنه} قال السدي:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r2.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says they follow the best of what they are commanded and act on it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r2.anchor: قال السدي: أحسن ما يؤمرون فيعملون به.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r3.claim: One view points to the Qur'an's mention of retaliation and forgiveness, with forgiveness the better of the two.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو أن الله تعالى ذكر في القرآن الانتصار من الظالم وذكر العفو، والعفو أحسن الأمرين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r4.claim: Another view says they choose obligatory acts over dispensations when the Qur'an mentions both.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r4.anchor: وقيل: ذكر العزائم والرخص فيتبعون الأحسن وهو العزائم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r5.claim: A further view says they hear Qur'an and other speech and follow the Qur'an.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r5.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون القرآن وغير القرآن فيتبعون القرآن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Bakr believed, then ʿUthmān and the named Companions asked him about it and believed; the verse was revealed about them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: آمن أبو بكر بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاءه عثمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r7.claim: The commentary concludes that all these explanations are good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r7.anchor: فآمنوا، فنزلت فيهم (1) : "فبشر عباد الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه" وكله حسن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says the two verses concern Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who professed God's oneness before Islam; the best word is lā ilāha illā Allāh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p112#4/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: نزلت "والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت" الآيتان،

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r8.claim: The explicit description replaces a pronoun for those shunning ṭāghūt, showing their discernment of truth and preference for better courses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r8.anchor: وضع فيه الظاهر موضع ضمير { الذين اجتنبوا }

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r9.claim: God guides them to His religion; guidance comes through God’s act and the soul’s acceptance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r9.anchor: أولئك الذين هداهم الله } لدينه. { وأولئك هم أولوا الألبب

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r10.claim: Sound minds are free of the competing influence of fancy and habit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:16-18/r10.anchor: العقول السليمة عن منازعة الوهم والعادة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r7.claim: They listen wholeheartedly to speech from any speaker, rather than stubbornly attending to one thing and rejecting the rest without evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r7.anchor: أي هذا الجنس من كل قائل ليسوا جفاة عساة إذا أقبلوا على شيء أعرضوا عن غيره بغير دليل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r8.claim: After assessing what they hear, they follow its best with full resolve, guided by reason rather than a lower desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r8.anchor: أي بكل عزائمهم بعد انتقاده : { أحسنه } بما دلتهم عليه عقولهم من غير إلى أدنى هوى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r9.claim: The verse clearly urges the People of the Book to follow this Qur'an: all revealed books are good, but the Qur'an is best in expression, meanings, and arrangement.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r9.anchor: فإن كتب الله كلها حسنة , وهذا القرآن أحسنها كلاما , ويعاني ونظاما

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r10.claim: “Those” singles out people of exceptional aspiration and rank from among the chosen.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r10.anchor: مظهرا زيادة المحبة لهم والاهتمام بشأنهم بالتأكيد : { أولئك } أي العالو الهمة والرتبة خاصة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r11.claim: Naming God as guide emphasizes the greatness of their guidance and that access to Him is possible only through Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r11.anchor: محولا الأسلوب إلى الاسم الأعظم إشارة إلى عظيم هدايتهم , { هداهم الله } بما له من صفات الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r12.claim: Unlike the reference to the prophets in al-Anʿām, “those whom God guided” omits the object; here it is stated, making their guidance recur through the relative clause.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r12.anchor: فقال { أولئك الذين هدى الله } فحذف المفعول لتصير هدايتهم مكررة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r13.claim: Repeating “those” and adding “they” intensifies honor and exclusivity: they alone possess intellect purified of confusion.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p433/r13.anchor: أي خاصة { أولوا الألباب * } أي العقول الصافية عن شوب كدر

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r1.claim: The compiler says the verse was revealed after an unnamed group made a statement; the excerpt does not identify them or preserve what they said.
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r1.anchor: قالوا بها فانزل الله تعالى على نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه} الآية

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.claim: Qatada glosses turning to God as coming back to Him and says the best speech they follow is obedience to God.
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى} قال: أقبلوا إلى الله {فبشر عباد الذين يستمعون

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the best thing followed is the obedience God commanded the prophets.
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {فيتبعون أحسنه} قال: ما أمر الله تعالى النبيين عليهم السلام من الطاعة

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r6.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says three things make him glad to live: prostrating to God, sitting with people who select good speech as they select good fruit, and striving in God’s path.
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r6.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله {الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه} قال: لولا ثلاث يسرني أن أكون قد مت

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r7.claim: Jabir reports that after 15:44 was revealed, an Anṣari who had freed one of his seven slaves for each gate of Hell received this verse as glad tidings.
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r7.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: لما نزلت (لها سبعة أبواب

DURR-FULL:v7p217/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r8.claim: Abu Saʿid says the Prophet sent a herald to announce that whoever dies without associating anything with God enters Paradise; ʿUmar recalled him, fearing people would stop striving, and the Prophet contrasted hope in mercy with fear of punishment.
DURR-FULL:v7p217/r8.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال لما نزلت {فبشر عباد الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه} أرسل رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r6.claim: The definite ‘speech’ is generic: it includes guidance such as the Quran and the Messenger’s instruction, as well as misguiding fabrications; they follow what is best, which calls to truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r6.anchor: أي يستمعون الأقوال مما يدعو إلى الهدى مثل القرآن وإرشاد الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r7.claim: Aḥsan here does not rank one good saying above another; it intensifies the quality, as in Joseph’s ‘prison is dearer’ at 12:33.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r7.anchor: فاسم التفضيل هنا ليس مستعملا في تفاوت الموصوف به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r8.claim: God praises them as discerning guidance from error, wisdom from illusions, and real proofs from sophistry; following the best speech points toward their receiving God’s guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p365/r8.anchor: أثنى الله عليهم بأنهم أهل نقد يميزون بين الهدى والضلال والحكمة والأوهام نظار في الأدلة الحقيقية نقاد للأدلة السفسطائية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r1.claim: The first clause is a fresh sentence that draws attention; the demonstrative singles out the people and highlights their deserving divine care because of the qualities just listed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r1.anchor: مستأنفة لاسترعاء الذهن لتلقي هذا الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r2.claim: Arabic discourse uses a demonstrative after descriptions to emphasize a judgment: it may point to the subject, as here, or to the predicate, as in 38:55.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r2.anchor: والإتيان باسم الإشارة عقب ذكر أوصاف أو أخبار طريقة عربية في الاهتمام بالحكم والمحكوم عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r3.claim: Defining both parts restricts guidance to them in an specifying, additional sense, as distinct from those who lost themselves and their families.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r4.claim: God’s guidance means He created souls receptive to the Prophet’s guidance; they wholeheartedly listened and sought His approval and rescue from wrath, rather than merely receiving commands available to all.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r4.anchor: بأن خلق الله نفوسهم قابلة للهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r5.claim: God’s guidance here does not mean simply directing guidance commands to them, since those who ignored the Quran also received that address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r5.anchor: وليس المراد بهدي الله إياهم أنه وجه إليهم أوامر إرشاده لأن ذلك حاصل للذين خوطبوا بالقرآن فأعرضوا عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r6.claim: The second clause attributes receptivity to God-given, sound intellects naturally inclined to truth over custom and falsehood; people differ in how quickly they reach guidance, with Khadīja, Abū Bakr, and ʿAlī believing at the first call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r6.anchor: بما فطرهم الله عليه من عقول كاملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r7.claim: The separating pronoun, possessive ‘people of,’ definite ‘intellects,’ and repeated demonstrative signal fully rooted understanding and distinguish them; ‘intellects’ is not generic because all rational people have some.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p366/r7.anchor: فليس التعريف فيه تعريف الجنس لأن جنس الألباب ثابت لجميع العقلاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r1.claim: Guidance requires an agent and a recipient: God is the agent, while the people of intellect are receptive; the second clause carries the same restriction as the first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r1.anchor: تنبيه على أن حصول الهداية لا بد له من فاعل وقابل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r2.claim: Praise for following the best speech honors inquiry and argument that distinguish truth from falsehood and right from error, close off doubt, and expose sophistry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r2.anchor: على شرف النظر والاستدلال للتفرقة بين الحق والباطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r3.claim: Reasoning needed to acquire sound belief is an individual duty, measured by each person’s capacity; deeper inquiry into Islamic law, its proofs and purposes, and sound social practice is a collective duty and excellence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r3.anchor: واجب على الأعيان وهو ما يكتسب به الإعتقاد الصحيح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r4.claim: Collective inquiry includes fiqh and understanding objectives in worship, transactions, and social etiquette, sustaining the Muslim community and answering deceivers, extremists, and heretics.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r4.anchor: والفقه في ذلك والفهم فيه والتهمم برعاية مقاصده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r5.claim: This principle calls for selecting the soundest proofs and most effective arguments without flaw by refining the sciences and their books; one should take the best from each science.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r5.anchor: بدون اختلال ولا اعتلال بتهذيب العلوم ومؤلفاتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r6.claim: A saying applies the verse as an instruction to take the best from every field of knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r6.anchor: قيل : خذوا من كل علم أحسنه أخذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verses were revealed about Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who avoided idol worship in pre-Islamic times and followed the best teaching that reached them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r7.anchor: وعن ابن زيد نزلت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر الغفاري وسلمان الفارسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p367/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the good-news passage was revealed about ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn Zayd, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who came to Abū Bakr after his conversion, heard his testimony, and believed.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r12.claim: The praise applies generally to all kinds of speech: these people have insight and sound judgment, weighing what they hear and following its best.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r12.anchor: كلام عام في جميع الأقوال، وإنما القصد الثناء على هؤلاء ببصائر هي لهم وقوام في نظرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r13.claim: One group says the best speech is God's Book: when people hear other statements and the Qur'an, they follow the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r13.anchor: فقالت فرقة: أحسن القول كتاب الله، أي إذا سمعوا الأقاويل وسمعوا القرآن اتبعوا القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r14.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r14.claim: Another group takes “the speech” as the Qur'an and its best as its commands to pardon, forbear, and endure patiently.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r14.anchor: وقالت فرقة: القول هو القرآن وأحسنه ما فيه من عفو وصفح واحتمال على صبر ونحو ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r15.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r15.claim: Qatāda says the best speech is obedience to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r15.anchor: وقال قتادة: أحسن القول طاعة الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r16.claim: He calls these particular readings examples, preferring his broad account, which encompasses them all.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p525/r16.anchor: وهذه أمثلة وما قلناه أولا يعمها

BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.claim: The Messenger gives glad tidings in this world; angels give them in the afterlife, which follows from the worldly good news.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r3.anchor: تبشير من لسان الرسول عليه السلام ، وهو تبشير في الدنيا.

BURSEVI:v8p67/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r5.speaker: المهدوي
BURSEVI:v8p67/r5.claim: Al-Mahdawi reports that the verse concerned Uthman, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Saad, Said, Talha, and al-Zubayr, who asked Abu Bakr about his faith and then believed.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r5.anchor: قيل : إن الآية نزلت في عثمان بن عفان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد وسعيد وطلحة والزبير حين سألوا

BURSEVI:v8p67/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r6.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p67/r6.claim: On that occasion, listening meant hearing Abu Bakr, and the best they followed was the declaration that there is no god but God.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r6.anchor: فيكون المعنى : يستمعون القول من أبي بكر ، فيتبعون أحسنه ، وهو قول لا إله إلا الله ، كما في "كشف الأسرار"

BURSEVI:v8p67/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67/r8.claim: Bursevi allows a broad reading: they hear any speech, Qur'an or otherwise, and follow its best through faith and good works; Qur'an is the best discourse.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى : يستمعون القول مطلقا قرآنا كان ، أو غيره ، فيتبعون أحسنه بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

BURSEVI:v8p67/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r9.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p67/r9.claim: Al-Raghib glosses following the best as following what is furthest from doubt.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r9.anchor: وقال الراغب في "المفردات" : فيتبعون أحسنه ؛ أي : الأبعد من الشبهة

BURSEVI:v8p67/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67/r10.speaker: بحر الحقائق
BURSEVI:v8p67/r10.claim: Bahr al-Haqaiq takes speech broadly to include God's, angels', humans', Satan's, and the self's; humans may speak truth or falsehood, good or bad, while Satan calls to sins.
BURSEVI:v8p67/r10.anchor: (ودر بحر الحقائق فرموده كه قول اعم است ازسخن خدا وملك وانسان وشيطان ونفس

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r1.claim: The examples say washing each limb once is good and washing three times is better; matching an injury is good, kindness is better; prayer or silent return is permissible, but glorifying while doing so is better.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r1.anchor: وإن غسل أعضاءه في الوضوء مرة مرة ، فهو حسن ، وإن غسلها ثلاثا ثلاثا ، فهو أحسن.

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r2.claim: This is compared with God's command to Moses to take revelation firmly and have his people take its best, and with the command to follow the best revelation.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r2.anchor: الآية قوله عز وجل لموسى عليه السلام : {فخذها بقوة وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها}

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.claim: Some say listeners follow God's speech and practice its best, especially Qur'anic pardon, forgiveness, and patience with harm; all Qur'an is good, while the best depends on the person acting.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى ما قال بعضهم : يستمعون قول الله ، فيتبعون أحسنه ويعملون بأفضله ، وهو ما في القرآن من عفو وصفح

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.claim: Al-Ashari and some leading scholars deny that one part of Qur'an is intrinsically better than another, since all is God's speech and ranking could imply inferiority elsewhere.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r4.anchor: ذهب الإمام أبو الحسن الأشعري رحمه الله وبعض الأئمة الأعلام إلى المنع ؛ لأن الجميع كلام الله

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.speaker: المحققون
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.claim: The preferred view is that God's speech about Himself is better than speech about other subjects; al-Ikhlas exceeds al-Masad for its mention of God's unity and attributes, while al-Masad has only the merit of God's speech.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r5.anchor: وذهب آخرون من المحققين ، وهو الحق كلام الله في الله أفضل من كلامه في غيره ، فقل هو الله أحد أفضل من تبت يدا أبي لهب

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.claim: Reports assigning special virtue and abundant reward to particular chapters and verses are too numerous to count.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r6.anchor: والأخبار الواردة في فضائل القرآن وتخصيص بعض السور والآيات بالفضل وكثرة الثواب في تلاوتها لا تحصى.

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.speaker: الغزالي
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.claim: In Jawhar al-Quran, al-Ghazali asks how some passages can be nobler if all are God's speech, then cites Prophetic descriptions of Yasin, al-Fatiha, the Throne Verse, and al-Ikhlas.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r7.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي رحمه الله في "جوهر القرآن" : كيف يكون بعض الآيات والسور أشرف من بعض مع أن الكل كلام الله

BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.claim: Those hesitant to rank verses can understand Prophetic phrases such as best surah as referring to reward: the eternal speech is equal in merit, with difference in reward rather than in God's speech itself.
BURSEVI:v8p67#3/r8.anchor: ومن توقف في تعديل الآيات أول قوله عليه السلام أفضل سورة وأعظم سورة أراد في الأجر والثواب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r3.claim: Following the best means understanding what one hears and acting on it, as Moses was told to take the Torah firmly and command his people to take its best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r3.anchor: أي: يفهمونه ويعملون بما فيه، كقوله تعالى لموسى حين آتاه التوراة: {فخذها بقوة وأمر قومك يأخذوا بأحسنها}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r4.claim: Those who listen and follow the best are guided by God in this life and the next, with sound minds and upright natural dispositions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p90#3/r4.anchor: أي: ذوو العقول الصحيحة، والفطر المستقيمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r7.claim: They are discerning in religion, distinguishing good from better and choosing the more excellent option.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r7.anchor: أن يكونوا نقادا في الدين يميزون بين الحسن والأحسن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r8.claim: When duty competes with recommendation they choose duty; between the permissible and recommended they choose the latter for greater divine reward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r8.anchor: اختاروا الواجب ، وكذلك المباح والندب ، حراصا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r9.claim: The principle also covers choosing the most firmly supported and best evidenced school of law after examination.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r9.anchor: واختيار أثبتها على السبك وأقواها عند السبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r10.claim: He warns against blind imitation, illustrating it with a poet’s image of a tethered camel that simply follows.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r10.anchor: ولا تكن مثل عير قيد فانقادا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r11.claim: One interpretation is that they hear the Qur’an and other speech, then follow the Qur’an.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r12.claim: Another interpretation is that they hear God’s commands and choose the better course, such as forgiveness over retaliation and discreet charity over public charity (2:237, 2:271).

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this describes a person who hears good and bad in a gathering, recounts the best, and withholds the rest.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p122/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هو الرجل يجلس مع القوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r11.speaker: مقاتل ويحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r11.claim: Muqatil and Yahya ibn Sallam say “the saying” means God's Book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r11.anchor: أحدهما : أن القول كتاب الله , قاله مقاتل ويحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says they had no divine scripture and listened to earlier communities' sayings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r12.anchor: الثاني : أنهم لم يأتهم كتاب من الله ولكن يستمعون أقاويل الأمم , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r13.claim: Qatada says they follow obedience to God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says they follow the testimony that no god exists but God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r14.anchor: الثاني : لا إله إلا الله ، قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r15.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r15.claim: Al-Suddi says they follow the best of what they were commanded.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r15.anchor: الثالث : أحسن ما أمروا به , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r16.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r16.claim: Al-Naqqash says they choose Islam after hearing Muslims and polytheists.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r16.anchor: اتبعوا أحسنه وهو الإسلام , حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas says to transmit the best part of a report and withhold its worst.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r17.anchor: فلا يتحدث به , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r18.claim: A further possibility is choosing strict duties over dispensations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r18.anchor: ويحتمل سادسا : أنهم يستمعون عزما وترخيصا فيأخذون بالعزم دون الرخص

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says it concerns Zayd ibn Amr, Abu Dharr, and Salman, who avoided idolatry before Islam and followed reason's best.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p119#2/r19.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد : نزلت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر الغفاري وسلمان الفارسي

MUQATIL:39:17-18/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r4.claim: The saying they hear is the Qur’an.

MUQATIL:39:17-18/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r5.claim: They follow the Qur’an’s best part, obedience to God, rather than prohibited acts; this is obedience in what God revealed.
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r5.anchor: يعنى أحسن ما فى القرآن من طاعة الله عز وجل، ولا يتبعون المعاصى

MUQATIL:39:17-18/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r6.claim: God guided them to His religion.

MUQATIL:39:17-18/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r7.claim: They are people of understanding because they follow God’s commands and prohibitions instead of evil attributed to others.
MUQATIL:39:17-18/r7.anchor: يعنى أهل اللب والعقل حين يستمعون فيتبعون أحسنه من أمره ونهيه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r1.claim: The listeners are the people just described; the overt noun replaces a pronoun to require that they combine avoidance of false worship and repentance with this discerning quality.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r1.anchor: هم الذين اجتنبوا وأنابوا وإنما أراد بهم أن يكونوا مع الاجتناب والانابة على هذه الصفة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r2.claim: They act as discerning judges in religion, choosing the obligatory over the recommended and, among permitted and recommended acts, what is closer to God and more rewarding.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r2.anchor: نقادا فى الدين يميزون بين الحسن والأحسن والفاضل والأفضل فإذا اعترضهم أمران واجب وندب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r3.claim: Alternatively, they hear the Qur'an and other speech and follow the Qur'an.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r3.anchor: أو يستمعون القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r4.claim: Alternatively, they follow the best of God's commands, such as choosing pardon instead of retaliation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r4.anchor: أو يستمعون أوامر الله فيتبعون أحسنها نحو القصاص والعفو ونحو ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r5.claim: Alternatively, in conversation they relate its best parts and refrain from repeating the rest.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r5.anchor: أو يستمعون الحديث مع القوم فيه محاسن ومساو فيحدث بأحسن ما سمع ويكف عما سواه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p51/r6.claim: Those guided by God and called people of intellect are the ones who put their reason to use.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says such a person hears good and bad, shares the good, and refrains from repeating the bad.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو الرجل يسمع الحسن والقبيح فيتحدث بالحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r14.claim: One view says they hear the Qur’an and other speech, then follow the Qur’an.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r14.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r15.claim: Another view says they hear the Qur’an and the Messenger’s statements, follow the best and clearest rulings, and act on them.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r15.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون القرآن وأقوال الرسول فيتبعون أحسنه أي محكمه فيعملون به

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r16.claim: Another interpretation is that they hear strict rulings and permissions, then choose strictness over concession.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r16.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون عزما وترخيصا فيأخذون بالعزم دون الترخيص

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r17.claim: Another interpretation is that they hear the punishment due and the offer of pardon, and choose pardon.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r17.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون العقوبة الواجبة لهم والعفو فيأخذون بالعفو

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r18.claim: For the view that these are pre-Islamic monotheists, the best statement is “There is no god but God.”
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r18.anchor: وقيل: إن أحسن القول على من جعل الآية فيمن وحد الله قبل الإسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r19.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r19.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says the passage concerned Zayd, Abu Dharr, and Salman: they avoided idols before Islam and followed the best teaching that reached them.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r19.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: نزلت في زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبي ذر الغفاري وسلمان الفارسي

QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:17-18/r20.claim: God guided them to what pleases Him; they are people of understanding because they made use of their intellects.

QASHANI:39:17-21/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r3.claim: The sayings heard include strict rulings and dispensations, and obligatory and recommended acts, whether attributed to God or others.
QASHANI:39:17-21/r3.anchor: كالعزائم والرخص والواجب والمندوب في قول الحق والغير

QASHANI:39:17-21/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r4.claim: Following the best means choosing strict rulings over dispensations and obligations over recommendations, although each item of speech is true.
QASHANI:39:17-21/r4.anchor: كالعزائم دون الرخص والواجب دون المندوب والقول حق في الكل لا غير

QASHANI:39:17-21/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:17-21/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:17-21/r5.claim: God guides them by original guidance; their liberated inner cores distinguish sayings and receive verified meanings.
QASHANI:39:17-21/r5.anchor: إليه بنور الهداية الأصلية { وأولئك هم أولو الألباب } المميزون بين الأقوال

RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r5.claim: Razi identifies the servants to be given glad tidings as the ones who shunned taghut and returned to God; naming them explicitly ties wholehearted devotion to listening and following the best.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r5.anchor: الذين اجتنبوا وأنابوا لا غيرهم وهذا يدل على أن رأس السعادات

RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r6.claim: The explicit noun phrase replaces an expected pronoun to signal that the previous God-turned servants are the listeners who follow the best.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r6.anchor: على هذا الحرف ، ومنهم من قال

RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r7.speaker: منهم
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r7.claim: Another view broadens the promise: anyone who chooses the best in every matter joins the saved, avoiding a restriction that would exclude most people from mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v26p226#2/r7.anchor: ومنهم من قال إنه تعالى لما بين أن الذين اجتنبوا وأنابوا لهم البشرى وكان ذلك درجة عالية لا يصل إليها إلا الأولون

RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r1.claim: The verse makes guidance depend on hearing many claims and choosing the soundest; because hearing is shared by all, reason rather than hearing distinguishes the best and merits praise.
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r1.anchor: وذلك لأنه تعالى بين أن الهداية والفلاح مرتبطان

RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r2.claim: Religions can be assessed by detailed proofs and rebuttals, or first by comparing them and accepting what sound reason judges more excellent before detailed inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r2.anchor: قبل البحث عن الدلائل وتقريرها والشبهات وتزييفها

RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p227/r3.claim: Initial rational comparison favors affirming a living, knowing, powerful, wise, merciful God; divine sovereignty; God's unity and freedom from composition; independence from space and time; and the possibility of forgiveness.

RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r1.claim: Among prayers, Razi prefers the form with intention at the opening takbir, al-Fatiha, tranquility in the five postures, tashahhud, and ending with salutation over one lacking these features.

RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r2.claim: Although retaliation, blood money, and pardon are legislated, God encourages pardon as nearer to piety.

RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says this refers to a person who hears good and bad in a gathering, then relates the best report and leaves the rest.
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس / أن المراد منه الرجل

RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r4.claim: Guidance requires an agent and a recipient: God is the agent, while the human soul is the receptive locus, identified as the people of understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r4.anchor: أمر حادث ، ولا بد له من فاعل وقابل

RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r5.claim: The soul and its rational light can receive either true or false belief equally, so the recipient cannot itself cause one to prevail; as a body equally receptive to motion and rest cannot select either, God must cause guidance.

RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r6.claim: Appealing to a will does not solve the problem: the soul is also equally receptive to the contrary will, so it cannot originate the preference that produces guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v26p228/r6.anchor: فكذلك ذات العقل قابلة لإرادة مضادة لتلك الإرادة

STUDYQURAN:39:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r1.claim: IK explains that they understand the Word and act in accordance with it, like Moses’ instruction to hold firmly to the best of the Torah’s commandments.
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r1.anchor: Those who listen to the Word, then follow are those who understand it and act in accord with it (IK)

STUDYQURAN:39:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r2.claim: They possess intellect because they follow and act in accordance with revelation.
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r2.anchor: They are possessors of intellect because they follow and act in accord with revelation

STUDYQURAN:39:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r3.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r3.claim: Z reads following the most beautiful as distinguishing good from best and virtuous from most virtuous, then choosing what is closer to God and earns greater reward.
STUDYQURAN:39:18/r3.anchor: chooses the best or most virtuous course of action, desiring what is closer to God and what merits greater reward (Z)

TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r2.claim: The Prophet is told to announce good news to servants who hear speakers and follow the most rightly guided speech toward God's oneness and obedience, leaving speech without guidance.
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r2.anchor: ويتركون ما سوى ذلك من القول الذي لا يدل على رشاد، ولا يهدي إلى سداد

TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the best speech is obedience to God.

TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says they follow the best of what they are commanded and then act on it.
TAB-FULL:v20p184#2/r4.anchor: السدي، في قوله: {فيتبعون أحسنه} [الزمر: 18] قال: «أحسن ما يؤمرون به فيعلمون به»

TAB-FULL:v20p185/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r1.claim: Ulū al-albāb are people of intellect and understanding.
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r1.anchor: هداهم الله بغير كتاب ولا نبي» {وأولئك هم أولو الألباب}

TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd reports from his father that these verses concerned Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr, and Salmān, who professed God's oneness and rejected idols before Islam, without a book or prophet.
TAB-FULL:v20p185/r2.anchor: ابن زيد، في قوله: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها. . .} [الزمر: 17] الآيتين " حدثني أبي أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا في ثلاثة نفر

SULAMI:v2p195/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195/r1.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
SULAMI:v2p195/r1.claim: Jesus describes the best companion as one whose sight reminds you of God and whose deeds make you desire the afterlife.
SULAMI:v2p195/r1.anchor: قال عيسى عليه السلام : من يذكركم الله رؤيته ويرغبكم في الآخرة عمله وقد قال الله تعالى :

SULAMI:v2p195/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p195/r2.claim: The verse honors Muhammad: although all prophetic teaching is good, the best address belongs to him; his station was established before creation and he leads in every spiritual rank.
SULAMI:v2p195/r2.anchor: ولما وقعت له صحبة التمكين ومقارنة الاستقرار قبل خلق الكون ظهرت عليه الأنوار في الأحوال كان معه احسن الخطاب

SULAMI:v2p195/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v2p195/r3.claim: The Prophet calls his community last in earthly existence but first in the primordial address and in precedence at the holy station.
SULAMI:v2p195/r3.anchor: ألا تراه صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ' نحن الآخرون السابقون يوم القيامة ' . يعني الآخرين وجودا السابقين في الخطاب الأول

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r8.claim: Given the following phrase about acting on speech, al-qawl means speech with some connection to action; its best form gives the surest guidance to truth and sincere counsel.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r8.anchor: والمراد بالقول بقرينة ما ذكر من الإتباع ماله نوع ارتباط ومساس بالعمل

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r9.claim: People drawn to beauty move from good to better when they encounter it; choosing only the good when a better option exists shows they were not responding to goodness itself.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r9.anchor: والإنسان إذا كان ممن يحب الحسن وينجذب إلى الجمال

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r10.claim: Following the best means pursuing truth and guidance: choose truth over falsehood and the more rightly guided course over the less guided one.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r10.anchor: فكلما دار الأمر بين الحق والباطل والرشد والغي اتبعوا الحق والرشد وتركوا الباطل والغي

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r11.claim: They listen hoping to find truth and fearing they may miss it; they do not dismiss speech on first hearing to follow their own desires without reflection and understanding.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r11.anchor: ولا يردون قولا بمجرد ما قرع سمعهم اتباعا لهوى أنفسهم من غير أن يتدبروا فيه ويفقهوه

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r12.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r12.claim: One view limits the phrase to hearing the Quran and other speech, then following the Quran; the author rejects this as an unsupported restriction.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد باستماع القول واتباع أحسنه استماع القرآن وغيره واتباع القرآن

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r13.claim: Another view restricts it to choosing the best divine commands, such as pardon over retribution or private over public almsgiving; the author likewise calls this unsupported specification.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r13.anchor: وقيل المراد استماع أوامر الله تعالى واتباع أحسنها كالقصاص والعفو فيتبعون العفو

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r14.claim: This trait is God's general guidance: seeking truth and being ready to follow it wherever found, the basis to which all detailed guidance to divine truths leads.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r14.anchor: هذه الصفة هي الهداية الإلهية وهذه الهداية أعني طلب الحق والتهيؤ التام لاتباع الحق أينما وجد

TABATABAI:39:16-18/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r15.claim: Those with sound intellects are guided to truth; their sign is following truth.
TABATABAI:39:16-18/r15.anchor: ويستفاد منه أن العقل هو الذي به الاهتداء إلى الحق وآيته صفة اتباع الحق

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r10.claim: They follow speech most worthy of acceptance and action, and most guiding to truth.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r10.anchor: أي أولاه بالقبول والعمل به وأرشده إلى الحق

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r11.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r11.claim: Al-Suddī says they follow and act on the best of what they are commanded.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: فيتبعون أحسن ما يؤمرون به ويعملون به عن السدي

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r12.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r12.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ names thirst in midday heat, night prostration, and companions who select the best speech like fine dates as three reasons to live.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r12.anchor: وروي عن أبي الدرداء قال لولا ثلاث ما أحببت أن أعيش يوما واحدا الظمأ بالهواجر

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r13.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj says they hear Qurʾān and other speech, then follow the Qurʾān.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه يستمعوه القرآن وغيره فيتبعون القرآن عن الزجاج

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r14.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r14.claim: They hear acts of obedience and permissible matters in Qurʾān and Sunna and choose the more virtuous, more rewarded option, such as pardon over lawful retaliation.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: يستمعون ما في القران والسنة من الطاعات والمباحات فيتبعون الطاعة التي هي أحسن

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r15.claim: God guided them and they followed the guidance to truth.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r15.anchor: أي هؤلاء الذين هذه صفتهم هم الذين هداهم الله فاهتدوا به إلى الحق

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r16.claim: They are people of intellect who have put their reason to use.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r16.anchor: أي ذوو العقول الذين انتفعوا بعقولهم

TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says the verses came down about three pre-Islamic monotheists: Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Abū Dharr, and Salmān al-Fārisī.
TABRISI:39:17-19#2/r17.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: نزل قوله { والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت } الآيتين في ثلاثة نفر

THALABI:v8p227/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p227/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v8p227/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda says he would value three things: thirst during the hottest days, prostration at night, and companions who select the best speech as one selects choice dates.
THALABI:v8p227/r1.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء: لولا ثلاث ما أحببت أن أعيش يوما واحدا: الظما بالهواجر، والسجود في جوف الليل، ومجالسه أقوام ينتقون من خير الكلام

THALABI:v8p227/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p227/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p227/r2.claim: Qatada says the best speech is obedience to God.

THALABI:v8p227/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p227/r3.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v8p227/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says it is what people hope for and then act upon.
THALABI:v8p227/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: أحسنه ما يرجون به فيعملون به.

THALABI:v8p227/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p227/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v8p227/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that these two verses concerned Zayd ibn Amr, Abu Dharr, and Salman al-Farisi, three pre-Islamic men who professed that there is no god but God.
THALABI:v8p227/r4.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت الآيتين: حدثني أبي: أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا في ثلاثة نفر كانوا في الجاهلية يقولون: لا إله إلا الله، وهم زيد بن عمرو

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r3.claim: People who turn to God after escaping false gods and misleading pressures can use reason and sound judgment to value and follow the best, truest words they hear.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r3.anchor: Kendi dışında veya içinde bu şekilde sahte tanrılar üretip onlara tapmaktan kurtularak Allah’a yönelen insanlar, içten veya dıştan gelebilecek her türlü saptırıcı telkinlerden, baskılardan ruhlarını kurtardıkları için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r4.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r4.claim: Razi says heard speech may be true or false, and rational proof is what distinguishes between them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r4.anchor: Râzî’ye göre duyulan bir söz doğru da yanlış da olabilir ve bunu ayıracak olan da aklî kanıttır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r5.claim: Razi generalizes reason’s authority to identify the best and truest across faith, worship, and law, urging critical thought and logical inference in every field.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r5.anchor: Râzî, bu âyetten yola çıkarak, aklın en iyi ve en doğru olanı ayırt etme konusundaki yetkisini iman, ibadet ve hukukî uygulamalara kadar bütün konulara genellemiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r6.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r6.claim: Razi adds that a person without intelligence and strong understanding cannot assemble the stated true knowledge in the mind.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:17/r6.anchor: Râzî’ye göre “Bir insan akıllı ve kavrayışı güçlü değilse belirtilen gerçek bilgileri zihninde toplaması da mümkün olmaz.”

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p368/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p368/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p368/r5.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that Abu Bakr believed and affirmed the Prophet, then Uthman, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn Zayd, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas followed; the verses concern them, and following the best speech points to what came from Abu Bakr.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p368/r5.anchor: قال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: إن أبا بكر الصديق - رضي الله عنه - آمن بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وصدقه

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r1.claim: Those guided to God’s oneness are people of sound understanding.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r1.anchor: أولئك الذين هداهم الله لتوحيده ، وأولئك الذين عقولهم غير معقولة

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.claim: Blind imitation prevents knowing what is best; one may hear truth and falsehood, but should not follow falsehood.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r1.anchor: وتدل على أن استماع الحق والباطل يحسن، وإن لم يحسن اتباع الباطل

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r3.claim: The description of those who follow truth promises them reward.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: أولئك أن متبع الحق موعود بالثواب

JISHUMI:v8p6052/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r6.claim: Piety and following truth are acts performed by the servant.
JISHUMI:v8p6052/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن التقوى واتباع الحق فعل العبد
